newsitem.title: GERMANY: German food body neutral on EU gene-maize move.
newsitem.headline: German food body neutral on EU gene-maize move.

text.p: German food industry institute BLL said a European Union decision to approve imports of genetically modified U.S. maize would be studied but there was no need to defend or criticise the ruling.
Scientific adviser Christiane Toussaint said the EU decision was based on three sets of scientic reports and closed a legislative gap as the maize was due to be imported.
BLL supplies scientific and legal services across the food industry.
"I don't know yet how relevant this ruling will be for food products," she said.
"I expect the labelling mentioned by the Commission will in the first line apply to feeds products."
Food products derived from the maize might or might not fall under the EU novel food law.
The European Commission on Wednesday approved Ciba Geigy AG's application for the market release of genetically modified maize, but said it would seek improved labelling.
Environmentalists oppose gene-modified maize and similar soybean products as a potential health risks and are stepping up a campaign to build consumer opposition.
In food products for human consumption, the EU novel food law requires labels on products containing "live" genetically modified cells.
It also requires labelling for other bio-engineered food which differs from conventional foods beyond "accepted limits of natural variation."
The EU has not yet communicated whether products derived from genetically altered maize would fall under this directive.
